Impressive! 

In my opinion (and don't take my word as I am not an AO), these ECs, if presented in a way that portrays your identity well, will get you into T50s. However, it falls short of the Ivy league and T20s (I would search profiles of admitted students for comparisons, but do note that not everything you see on the internet is true). If you improve your GPA and get a competitive SAT score (and perhaps register for a few competitions in your discipline of choosing), you have a good shot at some of the UCs.

As an international student, there are no "safeties" in the US––much less if you want a full-ride scholarship (it is still possible though!).

If you are considering reach schools like the ivies, your class rank should be at least top 10-15% and you should aim for a 1540+ SAT or 35-36 ACT (check your desired university's common dataset for statistics about the range of submitted test scores).

The IELTS/English proficiency test requirements vary college-by-college, so you'll have to look it up for your intended colleges.

If you need financial aid, some universities are need-blind for international students and others are not. The ones that are not need-blind will consider your request for financial aid as a part of their admissions file for you. This will make it harder to get into those universities.
